title: Lan Na
capsule: In this 1600–1762 window, Lan Na denotes Chiang Mai and the Ping-valley principalities under more than a century of Burmese suzerainty: Burmese-appointed vassal rulers governed after 1614, local autonomy returned after a 1727 revolt — most durably under Ong Kham (r. 1727–1759) — and Konbaung forces reimposed direct control after a seven-month siege in 1762–63.
